peri-megadim/1:ב: (ב) And know: on motzaei Shabbat one does not smell spices — if he intends to fulfill others, see siman 494 in Taz and Magen Avraham in what they wrote regarding Yom Kippur and Shabbat; even for us who are accustomed to smell, there is no berachah lebatalah, as Taz wrote in siman 494. Not so on motzaei Shabbat when one does not smell — he should not bless, lest the halacha is as the Mechaber wrote regarding Yom Kippur, and on motzaei Shabbat one is not obligated in spices at all — this is obvious. And see siman 494. And "Viten lecha" — they say in Musaf for chol or in Musaf for chol hamoed, but not in Musaf for Yom Tov, and not in Musaf for Yom Tov for chol. And Psalm 67 "Elohim yenatzeinu" and similar that they say in synagogue in Musaf for chol — also in Musaf for chol hamoed they say, but in Musaf for Yom Tov they do not, because it is a supplication; see Levush simanim 494 and 494 — see there; and so one should conduct.
